An initially 'flail limb' indicates a severe injury (axonotmesis/neurotmesis rather than simple neuropraxia). Even when elbow flexion returns, chronic muscle imbalance—where intact, powerful internal rotators/adductors (pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi, subscapularis) overpower denervated or weakened external rotators/abductors (deltoid, infraspinatus)—commonly leads to fixed shoulder contractures (adduction and internal rotation) by 18 months. The agents incorrectly generalized a favorable prognosis without accounting for this well-documented sequela, leading to a demonstrably wrong clinical prediction. This falls under the OTHER category as a factual/knowledge error in disease progression.
